question:
This aerial image was taken at an oblique angle, so building footprints look skewed and parallel streets appear to converge. Each candidate below is a 3x3 homography given row-major as nine numbers; applying it to the image is meant to restore a true orthographic (straight-down) view in which rectangular buildings become rectangular and parallel streets stay parallel. At most one candidate does this. Which one?
(A) [0.725236, -0.564786, 203.972, -0.0433812, 0.245416, 74.3141, -1.28978e-05, -0.000987185, 1]
(B) [2.63623, -0.7216, -130.173, 0.0421428, 1.83424, -257.192, 0.000858895, -0.000452934, 1]
(C) [1.70291, -0.598885, -206.576, 0.836041, 0.424439, -116.512, 0.000402338, -0.000834447, 1]
(D) None of the candidates produces a correct orthographic view.

Answer with only the correct option letter.

</tool_call>

After applying candidate (C), the resulting image [img3] still shows a skewed view. The land and vegetation appear stretched, and the natural features do not appear parallel or rectangular. This indicates that candidate (C) is also not correct.

Since candidates (A) and (B) either failed or did not produce the desired result, and candidate (C) also did not work, it is likely that none of the provided candidates produce a correct orthographic view.

Therefore, the correct answer is (D).
